ward-sign.notes:
meta: starter_level=S3; path=optional; skills=repeat-string,print-text,make-variable; solo=false; dictates=3,4; foreign_names=chalk; prereq_card=1A-07 many-lines-at-once
Spec 1P2. Letters go DOWN the post (one under another), so each row is one print and no row needs side-by-side glue. Checks: CP1/CP2 count rows that change between two reruns (ink '#' and ink '@'), so rows typed with █ are caught (CMB with ink); a row with a mark that is the same in both reruns is half typed (caught); the letter's own five ink rows (after the T's five) need a row with a gap between two marks, so a copied T, a column of marks or a filled block fails while any real O or R design passes; CP3 the border is the first line, not an ink row, stamped (a 1-3 character unit repeated), not typed as one literal, and repeated after the last ink row (a later side-quest line under the sign keeps it green); CP4 ink changed (near-miss name caught first) AND the printed letters use the new mark (ink changed after the letters fails). CP4 suggests `#` or `@` (or Mar'tu's pick ▓); any mark passes all five steps, `#`, `@`, `X`, `*` and even `=` (the reruns use their own marks, so the `=` border is never an ink row). CP5 one print with a triple-quoted string of 5+ non-blank rows, drawn with any key. The triple-quoted letter does not follow ink on purpose: CP5's pass line asks the student to notice that (the quotes rule again). Side quest (spec): sign the post in your hero's spell color, checked with a rerun (spell_color 'moth-grey'). Trial mode after a QC1 pass: premise + required output + the check table, from blank (site work).
